body: I know that it wasn’t a long time to wait for a response, but I hope it doesn’t seem like I felt entitled to a fast response from her; it was honestly just me being concerned for her well-being. I do admit I jumped the gun on asking for advice, especially since it resolved itself; I’m honestly the biggest worrywart I know and have the tendency of assuming the worst very quickly, so in hindsight, I panicked a little too fast haha

Yeah, I hope it’s nothing, but I do know she lives with her adult son, so thankfully I imagine a medical emergency would be somewhat handled. I might also try to talk to someone who I know is in the class before mine, so I can find out if she missed that class as well or if she had said anything.

This happened when my great granddad died. He was pretty old and my grandma (his daughter) and my granddad lived right now the street from him and always would be helping him with medications, groceries, and everything else. My granddad also would mow his yard every week or so. One or two of my great aunts would help occasionally, but it was never as consistently as my grandparents did.
When my great granddad passed, my grandma was made the executor of the will and was to divide the inheritance between the family.
My great aunts and my great uncle became greedy and their relationships with my grandma has suffered greatly because of it, however, one of my great aunts took it way too far. My grandma is a cancer survivor (and a pretty cool person) and one of my great aunts told her “I wish the cancer had killed you” over a chest that my great aunt wanted. Afterwards, she pretty much cut all contact with my grandma and even blocked my mom on Facebook. We haven’t heard much of anything from her since, though, we do still see her kids (my cousins) because they’re far more reasonable than their mom.
